robust

roh-BUST — stress the BUST; something robust is so strong it won't bust. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Robust is strong, healthy, and unlikely to fail or break down.

The bridge's robust design let it withstand decades of storms and heavy traffic.

Example

One laptop in the office has survived three drops down the stairs, a full cup of spilled coffee, and five years of daily travel. It still boots instantly and runs every program. Its owner has never once taken it in for repair.

Something built so strong and reliable that it resists failure is robust. Unlike 'big,' robustness is about strength and durability, not size.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

sturdy: Sturdy means solidly built so it will not wobble, tip, or snap — a sturdy ladder or table. Robust reaches beyond the build to performance under stress: a robust system keeps working through abuse and overload. Sturdy praises how a thing is made; robust praises how it holds up.

vigorous: Vigorous means strong, healthy, and full of active energy — a vigorous swimmer, a vigorous debate. Robust shares the health but centers on resistance to failure: a robust appetite or economy withstands whatever strains it. Vigorous is energy in motion; robust is strength that refuses to break down.

durable: Durable means able to survive long use and slow wear — durable boots last through years of walking. Robust means unlikely to fail even under sudden stress: a robust design shrugs off shocks, drops, and overloads. A durable thing outlasts time; a robust one outlasts abuse.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

frail: weak and delicate

flimsy: badly made and easily broken

Where it sits · how much stress it can take — sound → robust → unbreakable

sound vs. robust: Sound is weaker than robust — a sound structure is in good condition, while a robust one is actively powerful and built to shrug off stress.

unbreakable vs. robust: Unbreakable is stronger than robust: a robust phone case survives most drops, but an unbreakable one cannot be broken at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — robur-

root — robur-: oak; strength (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin robur named the oak tree, the ancient symbol of toughness. Something robust is literally 'as strong as oak' — solid, healthy, and hard to break.

Use the root in a new word: corroborate
